Offerings and sacrifices were made to the gods to win their favors. In BLOT, you are invited to make offerings during four simultaneous ceremonies honoring the Aesir, the powerful Nordic gods. In each round, you will attempt to win the favors of three out of four divinities - Balder, Loki, Odin, and Thor. At the end of the four rounds, the player who has collected the most Devotion points wins the game. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Turn 3 Concluding a Ceremony 4 Round End 5 Game End Overview Have the most points after 4 rounds and avoid gaining negative points Turn You have a number of options on your turn You can Start a Ceremony by placing onto a Ceremony Tile a card with a different colour (If you have to use the same colour as the Ceremony tile, you must prove this and show your hand to the other players before doing so, but can hide the values) You can Make an Offering by adding another card of the same colour as the initial one on a Ceremony Tile, the value doesn't matter (If you are unable to do this, you can either play a card of the Ceremony Tile's colour or play any other card) Concluding a Ceremony Once a Ceremony Tile has as many cards around it as the number of players, it is Concluded The winner of a Ceremony is either the highest card of the Ceremony Tile colour then the highest card of the initial placed card's colour (trump and lead) The winner takes all the cards which surround the Ceremony Tile and place them in a new layered stack in their scoring area, as such do not mix cards won at different ceremonies If the Ceremony tile was dark, flip it to its light side If the Ceremony tile was light, the winner chooses a Divinity to offer it to, these Divinities create scoring opportunities based on that colour Ceremony Tile Round End The round ends when all Ceremony Tiles have been assigned to Divinities If a player has not won any Ceremonies, they can neither win nor lose points Otherwise, every other player first gains 3 points per Ceremony Won then the Divinities will cause points to be gained or lost based on their conditions The Tally card is actually covering one of the Divinities, so once scoring is complete, first move this Tally one step to the right then flip all non-covered Divinities to their other scoring condition side Whoever won the last Ceremony of a round chooses who to go first next round, themself or someone else Game End The game ends at the end of the fourth round The player with the most points, wins! If tied, first the tied player who won the final Ceremony wins! If this is not the case, the tied player who gained the most points in a single round, wins! [Rating: 6/10] Weird game. In a good way. I have played so many "trick taking games with a twist!" lately that I almost wrote this off at first, but it turns out that there is actually still room for some innovation in this design space. Instead of the normal progression of trick taking, with each person playing a card and resolving the trick, BLOT will have multiple tricks going at once. It is possible that you have multiple cards in one trick and someone else has none.
